correctness.rationale: The projected vertex inner product is cos(theta)-(n·u)(n·v); in the angle-bisector coordinates, its negativity is exactly n_2^2+cos^2(theta/2)n_3^2<sin^2(theta/2). Integrating Haar normals gives the stated one-angle integral; acute-angle strict convexity follows by positive derivatives in x=sin^2(theta/2), reflection gives p(pi-theta)=1-p(theta), and disjointness of obtuse vertex events gives P=sum p. Strict Jensen for three acute input angles gives the equilateral minimum, while any source angle >=pi/2 contributes >=1/2 > the sharp equilateral value, confirmed by a rational nonnegative polynomial certificate in the proof. Restricted orthogonal projections realize any singular-value ratio (1,k) with 0<k<=1; every triangle has an acute projection of positive measure, so P<1, while flattening an angle to pi tends to P=1. Reconstructed normalization, equality and endpoints, not a finite empirical inference. Independent high-precision quadrature and 180000 independent random sphere normals verified the equilateral value and local sign law; the simulation is only corroboration.

final_claim: For a fixed nondegenerate Euclidean triangle T, a uniformly Haar-random two-plane shadow in R^3 is obtuse with probability P(T)=p(alpha)+p(beta)+p(gamma), where p is the explicit one-dimensional integral. P(T)>=3p(pi/3)=0.470339624536... with equality only for an equilateral T; its exact attainable range is [3p(pi/3),1).
